column1: # Why: with a general organism restriction (Bacteria OR Archaea OR Fungi),
# Primer-BLAST puts EVERY product it finds into the "target templates" column and
# leaves the "unintended" section empty. That was measured on all 22 pages.
# The fix: exclude the target's OWN taxon through the Entrez query, and then
# every product that remains is off target by definition.
# An empty taxid means no exclusion is applied and that target is written down as
# NOT TESTED. More than one taxid is written comma separated and each becomes its
# The exclusion IS APPLIED to universal primers too: exclude the domain, and every
# product that remains is a real off target one, such as a bacterial primer
# THE KEYS have to match the target name in the order list EXACTLY; a key that
# does not match silently produces NOT TESTED, which happened to two of them on
# 2026-08-10. THE TAXIDS WERE CONFIRMED against NCBI Taxonomy on 2026-08-10.
# THE RULE: the taxon to exclude is chosen by the MEASURED IDENTITY and not by
# the target's NAME, and it is widened to the narrowest taxon that CONTAINS the
# measured identity. In this project the name and the measured identity diverge
# in 78 of 100 bins, so going by the name would leave the target itself
# unexcluded and count its own hits as off target.

column3: gerekce
the genus Methanothrix, NCBI Taxonomy

M. soehngenii (2223) plus the GENUS Methanothrix (2222). All three member bins resolve only to GENUS level when measured, giving "Methanothrix" and no species name. Excluding 2223 alone would have counted the target's own bins as off target. The cost: this layer CANNOT tell another Methanothrix species apart; species level separation is measured by layers 2 and 3.
the genus Methanosarcina, NCBI Taxonomy

M. mazei plus M. soligelidi plus the "Methanosarcina sp." node (2213): one member bin resolves only to genus level when measured. The pair targets BOTH species, 2209 and 1036677, so both are excluded. The genus (2207) is NOT excluded: catching another Methanosarcina species IS OFF TARGET and has to stay visible.

The genus Methanomassiliicoccus (1080709) plus the FAMILY Methanomassiliicoccaceae (1577788). The member bin's measured identity stops at family level; at genus level the measured identity is an unnameable lineage at 99.23 per cent. The genus is used rather than the species, because the name is not certain.
The GENUS Ca. Nitrosocosmicus: the measured identity is "Nitrocosmicus cf. oleophi", which is not a species. The old value 1826872, the species hydrocola, would have excluded a different species.
The FAMILY Synergistaceae: the measured identity is an unnameable Synergistaceae. The old value 1197717, the species Cloacibacillus porcorum, would not have excluded the target at all.

The order Planctomycetales: the MEASURED identity is "Planctomycetales bacterium". The old value 456827, Ca. Cloacimonas, WAS WRONG: it had been chosen by Kraken's NAME, so the target itself went unexcluded and its own hits counted as off target.
The GENUS Sphaerochaeta: the measured identity is an unnameable lineage at 95.49 per cent. The genus is used rather than the species.

Petrimonas (307628) plus Proteiniphilum (294702). MEASURED: two of the three member bins are an "unnameable lineage" whose nearest records end in Proteiniphilum, and only one comes out as "Petrimonas sp.". In this sample Kraken's Petrimonas against Proteiniphilum distinction corresponds to a single unnamed Bacteroidales lineage, which is also consistent with the verdict that the Proteiniphilum genus target is not in the sample. Both are excluded together.

the order Methanomicrobiales, NCBI Taxonomy

Methanosarcinales (94695) plus Methanotrichales (2905377). MEASURED on 2026-08-10: NCBI has TAKEN Methanothrix OUT of Methanosarcinales and moved it under its own order Methanotrichales (the lineage: Methanomicrobia; Methanotrichales; Methanotrichaceae; Methanothrix). With 94695 alone, the target's own Methanothrix members would have counted as OFF target. The old reasoning, that 94695 covers Methanothrix, IS NO LONGER TRUE; it had been written from memory and came out once the lineage was pulled. The order Methanosarcinales was CONFIRMED on 2026-08-10: 2206 was the FAMILY Methanosarcinaceae, and because the member set holds Methanothrix 2223 which sits under Methanotrichaceae, excluding by family would have been incomplete.

Methanotrichales (2905377) WAS ADDED, because Methanothrix sits there. EVERY methanogen order is listed (Methanobacteriales, Methanococcales, Methanomicrobiales, Methanosarcinales, Methanopyrales, Methanocellales, Methanomassiliicoccales, Methanonatronarchaeales). The methanogens are not one taxon but spread across several orders; excluding Archaea instead would have HIDDEN the primer catching a non-methanogen archaeon. Every product that remains is off target.
